subject: Privilege playbook & follow-up from discovery call: data access, retention, break-glass

Subject: Privilege playbook & follow-up from discovery call: data access, retention, break-glass

Hi Sam / Emily,

Thanks for taking the call today — good to meet you both. Quick recap from my side and a couple of qualification questions so we can route the right folks:

Recap (from our call)
- BlueLine will evaluate Redwood for patient-facing summarization and clinical documentation features.
- Key privacy asks: strict PII handling, short retention on generated content, support access controls for logs, and data residency in us-east.
- Procurement expects an initial pilot with ~2M tokens/month and possibility to expand.

Open items we need to confirm before I loop security and solutions:
1) PII scope — do you consider any PHI identifiers beyond name/DOB/SSN (e.g., device IDs, MRN) as sensitive for this pilot?
2) Retention target — you mentioned "minimal" retention; can you confirm a target (30/90/365 days)?
3) Support access model — do you require break-glass approvals tied to named individuals, or would a time-limited JIT support token be acceptable?

Next steps: if you can confirm the three items above I will:
- Share our concise RBAC matrix and support break-glass workflow for your security review (low/no PII access by default).
- Have Neha (security) and Marissa (customer success) join for a short follow-up to map to your procurement checklist.

I've put a one-page checklist attached we often use for pilots; feel free to fill and return.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

Subject: Re: Privilege playbook & follow-up from discovery call: data access, retention, break-glass

Connor,

Thanks for the clear recap. Short answers below, plus attaching our standard security questionnaire (see attachment). We also looped legal for any contract-level language.

1) PII/PHI scope: we consider names, DOB, SSN, MRN, and device IDs as PHI for this pilot. Also any free-text clinical notes that can link to a patient are sensitive.
2) Retention: pilot requirement is 90 days for derivative logs; for raw audit logs we may need 1 year. We can discuss longer-term retention once we move past pilot.
3) Support access: we prefer a JIT break-glass with approval via our PagerDuty + ticketing system. Named standing access is disallowed.

Also: data residency must remain in us-east for the pilot. Can you confirm whether your hosted Redwood API has a us-east-only tenancy for customer data and logs?

Attached: security_questionnaire_BlueLine.pdf

Sam Perez
Director, Clinical Informatics | BlueLine Health

Connor / team / Sam,

Thanks — reviewed the questionnaire and BlueLine's quick notes. Below is a draft one-page playbook we can send to BlueLine for the pilot. Please review and call out anything missing.

Redwood pilot playbook (summary)
- Data residency: Tenant data and logs for the pilot will be stored in the us-east region only. We will provision a region-scoped tenancy and document the storage locations in the SOW.

- RBAC (minimal roles to propose)
  * Viewer: read-only access to aggregated metrics and non-identifying logs (no PII).
  * Analyst: can view transformed derivatives (de-identified summaries) but cannot export raw notes.
  * Operator: can restart inference jobs, view operational metrics, and see anonymized traces; cannot access PII.
  * Support-BreakGlass: time-limited, JIT elevated access only after customer-approved PagerDuty ticket; scoped to a single session and audited.
  * Admin: tenant admins designated by BlueLine (two named contacts) for config and account management.

- Break-glass workflow (high level)
  1) BlueLine opens a ticket in their system and approves via PagerDuty escalation.
  2) Support requests JIT token from Redwood console with an attached ticket id and approver name.
  3) JIT token grants Support-BreakGlass role for a bounded window (max 2 hours) and is logged.
  4) All session activity is recorded (command-level audit, query text masked at PII patterns) and preserved in audit logs.
  5) Post-session: automated email to BlueLine approvers and retention of the session record for 1 year (per their ask); derivative logs retained 90 days.

- PII handling
  * Inbound content is parsed for PII patterns; PII is redacted from derivative logs and replaced with stable pseudonyms where needed.
  * Raw input transcripts used for debugging can be retained only with explicit customer opt-in and are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys if required.

- Logging & retention
  * Operational logs (error traces, infra metrics): 90 days
  * Audit/session logs (support JIT sessions, commands): 1 year (customer requested)
  * Derivative outputs (summaries): 90 days by default, configurable via SOW

- Technical controls we will offer for pilot
  * Region-scoped tenancy for us-east
  * Customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest (optional)
  * Fine-grained RBAC tied to SCIM groups or SAML assertions
  * Immutable audit trail with tamper-evidence metadata

- Open questions for BlueLine (to confirm in follow-up)
  1) Acceptance of masked PII in diagnostic logs vs requiring full redaction.
  2) Maximum allowed JIT session window (we propose 2 hours).
  3) Whether BlueLine wants us to include session recording transcripts in the 1-year audit retention or retain only metadata + masked transcripts.

I'll convert this to a one-page PDF and drop back into the thread. If this looks good, Connor please schedule a 30-min follow-up with Sam and Emily and include Marissa for pilot onboarding.

-Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
